This is the live Alexa/Google voice-webhook handler (voice_commands is the production voice command dispatcher and a repeat churn hotspot). A resident asking their assistant to 'contact the manager' is read back a fabricated example.com address as if it were real contact info.

Distinct from the 2026-08-20 api-core finding on action_book_facility (voice-facility-contact-fabricated-success): different intent handler, different defect class — fabricated PII/contact data returned to the user rather than a fabricated booking-success.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:168 and :307 — alexa_webhook and google_actions_webhook take `mut rls: RlsConnection` as a handler argument, making a validated Property-Management principal a hard precondition for the handler body to run.

backend/crates/api-core/src/extractors/rls_connection.rs:229-232 — RlsConnection::from_request_parts first runs ValidatedTenantExtractor::from_request_parts; backend/crates/api-core/src/extractors/tenant.rs:135-137 — ValidatedTenantExtractor first requires AuthUser (a valid PM JWT Bearer token) and returns 401 when it is absent/invalid. backend/servers/api-server/src/lib.rs:339-342 — the router is nested at /api/v1/webhooks/voice with no auth-injecting middleware that supplies a synthetic tenant context, so nothing provides the JWT the extractor demands.

CONSEQUENCE: real Alexa / Google Assistant requests authenticate with a platform SIGNATURE (verified inside the handler at voice_webhooks.rs:172 via verify_alexa_signature and :312 via verify_google_request), never a PM JWT. The RlsConnection extractor therefore rejects every genuine platform request with 401 BEFORE the signature-verification and VoiceCommandProcessor logic ever executes — the two primary voice endpoints are unreachable by the callers they exist to serve, and the entire hardened Alexa/Google signature surface is dead code in production.

CORROBORATION (correct pattern): sibling signature-authenticated webhooks in backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/portal_webhooks.rs:318-321 take only State/HeaderMap/Bytes and require no JWT; and voice_webhooks.rs oauth_token_refresh at :694-707 documents that `voice_assistant_devices` is NOT RLS-bound and does its device lookup on RlsPool::acquire_public() (context-cleared) with an explicit ownership check — that is the pattern alexa_webhook/google_actions_webhook should use (authz is already done by authenticate_voice_user matching the presented voice token, voice_webhooks.rs:1574-1681).

WHY UNCAUGHT: the unit tests deliberately do not exercise the handler entrypoints — voice_webhooks.rs:1826-1838 states the four handlers holding a live DB connection are left to an integration harness — so the extractor never runs in-test and the reachability regression is invisible to the suite.

FIX DIRECTION: drop `RlsConnection` from alexa_webhook/google_actions_webhook and acquire the connection internally after signature verification via RlsPool::acquire_public() (mirroring oauth_token_refresh and portal_webhooks), keeping authenticate_voice_user as the authorization gate.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:172-178 — alexa_webhook returns on every error branch (signature failure :174, body parse :181, authenticate_voice_user :197, process_command :224/:246) WITHOUT calling rls.release().await, even though the RlsConnection was already extracted (a pooled connection acquired and RLS context set) before the body ran.

backend/crates/api-core/src/extractors/rls_connection.rs:197-220 — the Drop impl preserves correctness (it spawns spawn_clear_context to clear the RLS GUCs before the pooled connection is reused) BUT logs a WARN "RlsConnection dropped without calling release()" and spawns an extra task on every such drop.

INCONSISTENCY: google_actions_webhook DOES release on its verify-failure branch (voice_webhooks.rs:314) but NOT on its authenticate_voice_user (:331) or process_command (:361) error returns — the release discipline is applied unevenly across branches within the same file.

IMPACT: low — no cross-tenant leak (Drop clears context), but because these are public, attacker-reachable endpoints, a flood of failing requests (e.g. bad signatures) each spawns a cleanup task and emits a WARN, an avoidable log-spam / task-churn amplification. NOTE: this is partly subsumed by the reachability finding above — if the handlers are moved off RlsConnection to acquire_public(), these branches no longer hold an RlsConnection to release.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:412-415 — initializeAuth() (the mount-time effect) branch `if (storedUser && accessToken)` carries the comment 'Validate the token is not expired (basic check)' but then just calls setUser(storedUser). No expiry validation is performed: an expired access token persisted in localStorage is accepted verbatim and the app renders an authenticated session on cold boot.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:221-233 — decodeJwtPayload() already extracts the unverified JWT claims (used by deriveActiveRole) and could read `exp`, so the guard the comment promises is trivially implementable with an existing utility; it is simply not wired into the cold-boot path.

Impact/reachability: on every reload with a stale token the user is treated as authenticated until the first API call returns 401 and the axios response interceptor (lib/api.ts:218-221) fires onUnauthorizedCallback. During that window protected UI can flash and deriveActiveRole runs against an expired token. Self-recovering via the 401 flow (hence medium, not high), but the comment/code mismatch is a real auth-correctness gap on the app's core session-init path.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/marketplace/components/VerificationBadge.tsx:155-158 — same unguarded window in VerificationStatusBadge (status==='verified' && expiryDate && delta < 30d): a verified record whose expiryDate is in the past shows orange 'Expires: <date> (Soon)' rather than an expired state.
